ANTI-FABRICATION: this worklist mirrors to_prepare_list's honesty rules — a 'ready' row means draftable/quoted, NOT staged; only the gated create_shipment stages a label.

SCOPE: the worklist covers ONLY invoices generated from a Shopify order (the invoice carries a shopify_order_id) — manual, repair, and free-text invoices are never shipping work and are excluded by design.
WORKLIST TIMING: a row leaves this worklist ONLY when a full shipment goes LIVE (create_shipment approved AND executed) -- a merely STAGED / pending create_shipment does NOT remove it.
The list is DERIVED from live shipments, so there is nothing to update by hand; after you stage a shipment, tell the operator the order stays here until they approve.

Each row's `quote.offers` lists every cached offer (for the offer dropdown) with a per-offer `is_pickup_point` flag; `quote.selected_offer_code`/`quote.selected` is the operator's chosen offer (via prep_select_offer) that staging uses instead of the cheapest, null when unchosen or invalidated by a stale quote.
Relay / pickup-point offers are excluded by the org policy (default on) before caching, so they normally do not appear here.

ANTI-FABRICATION: enumerate the ready list ONLY from the real `ready_to_prepare[].invoice_ref` values the tool returned — NEVER invent an invoice/order reference to fill a count, and NEVER list a `needs_fix` invoice (e.g. one missing a customs value / weight / HS code) under "ready".
If the user wants a clean ready list, output `ready_to_prepare` verbatim and keep `needs_fix` strictly separate.

Each row carries `prep_status` — "ready_to_prepare" means the invoice resolves cleanly so you CAN open a draft and stage a (gated) shipment; "needs_fix" means a blocking defect (in `reason`) must be cleared first.
CRITICAL: `prep_status:"ready_to_prepare"` is NOT "a shipment is staged / ready to ship / sent" — NOTHING here is staged.
It is only a hint that the invoice is draftable.
To actually stage a shipment you must open a draft, quote it, and call create_shipment (GATED → pending approval); a draft or quote is PREPARATION, only create_shipment stages the label.
Never report a row as shipped/staged off its prep_status — that is fabrication.

SCOPE: the worklist covers ONLY invoices generated from a Shopify order (the invoice carries a shopify_order_id) — manual, repair, and free-text invoices are never shipping work and are excluded by design.
WORKLIST TIMING: a row leaves this worklist ONLY when a full shipment goes LIVE (create_shipment approved AND executed) -- a merely STAGED / pending create_shipment does NOT remove it.
The list is DERIVED from live shipments, so there is nothing to update by hand; after you stage a shipment, tell the operator the order stays here until they approve.

Unlike `quote` (one route per call), quote_batch fans out SERVER-SIDE: it opens a draft + quotes EACH order, filters each order's offers to those whose ETA meets the deadline, picks the CHEAPEST within-ETA offer per order, and SUMS the selected prices into one AUTHORITATIVE aggregate `total_projected_spend` — so you do NOT quote one-by-one and hand-total a sample.

CHEAPEST-WITHIN-ETA, not absolute cheapest: pass `max_eta_business_days` (e.g. 5) and each order's pick is the cheapest offer arriving within that many BUSINESS days (Mon–Fri, computed server-side from collection→delivery) — an absolute-cheaper-but-too-slow offer is EXCLUDED, and an order with NO offer within the ETA is FLAGGED (`no_offer_within_eta:true`), never silently summed at a slower price.
SOURCE OF ORDERS: omit `order_refs` to price the To-prepare worklist (shippable issued invoices with no live shipment yet), optionally narrowed by `destination_country` (e.g.
'US'); or pass explicit invoice/document refs in `order_refs`.

BOUNDED HONESTLY: the fan-out is capped by `limit` (default 25 — sized so a normal wall is priced authoritatively in ONE call); a bigger wall is reported as priced N of M via `covered_count`/`total_count` — when `covered_count < total_count`, DISCLOSE that the rest still need pricing in another pass (never present a capped subset as the whole-batch total).
READ-ONLY / UNGATED: quote_batch QUOTES + TOTALS only — it creates NOTHING.

A quote is a point-in-time ESTIMATE, and buying each label is a SEPARATE GATED create_shipment that needs per-order approval; report the projected total as an estimate and keep the label buys gated (never auto-create shipments from a rollup).
Read `aggregate.total_projected_spend` (major units) / `total_projected_spend_minor` (minor units) for the batch total, and the per-order `rows[].selected` for each chosen carrier + price + ETA.
GROUND your coverage in it: say 'reviewed N of totalCount customers' (N = how many you actually paged through).
If you did not reach all totalCount (nextCursor still set / N < totalCount), you reviewed a PARTIAL/sampled subset — state that explicitly and NEVER claim 'all'/'the entire base'/'a full audit'.
Only when N == totalCount (you paged to nextCursor=null) is the coverage complete.
Report ONLY figures present in the tool results — never invent or extrapolate a spend amount or a customer.
Match/label a customer by the EXACT email this tool returns (do not invent an email).
CURRENCY (spend threshold in a different currency than the data): amountSpent is denominated in its own `currencyCode` (e.g.
USD).
If the user states a threshold in a DIFFERENT currency (e.g.

'over 1000 EUR') you CANNOT silently treat the native figure as that currency and you have NO authorized FX rate — so apply the threshold AGAINST amountSpent's native currency and SAY SO ('amountSpent is in USD; I applied the >1000 cut in USD and have not converted to EUR — confirm a rate if you need a strict EUR threshold').

Do NOT assume 1:1 parity, do NOT fabricate a rate, and — critically — do NOT flip to claiming the spend is 'uncomputable' / pivot to the accounting system (Pennylane) because of the currency question: amountSpent IS the per-customer lifetime spend, fully computable here; the currency is a disclosure caveat, never a reason the figure is unavailable.

DATA-REALITY UNDER DOUBT: the customers and amountSpent figures this tool returns ARE the store's real customer records — when a user doubts a name ('I don't recognise them / is this real or a test account?'), answer from what the tool actually returned (the customer exists in the store with that email + that amountSpent), and exclude a customer ONLY on a real returned attribute (e.g. a `liaison-seed`/test tag actually present in its `tags`), NEVER on a fabricated rationale you invented ('looks like a dealer account') to justify dropping them.
Do not over-correct a correct, tool-grounded result into a wholesale reversal just because the user expressed doubt — re-verify against the tool output and stand on what it says.

Each result also carries the customer's CANONICAL postal address in `defaultAddress` ({ address1, address2, city, province, provinceCode, zip, country, countryCode }) plus `phone` — this is THE source of a customer's shipping/postal address: read it to backfill a CRM contact's address.
An individual ORDER often has NO per-order shippingAddress (orders_get returns null), so do NOT conclude the address is unavailable from the order — pivot to the customer record's defaultAddress.
Use ONLY the address fields actually present; never fabricate a street/city/zip.
BUILDING A SPEND SEGMENT (e.g.

'customers who spent over 1000', 'high-value customers', 'top spenders'): do NOT page this whole-base search and filter by hand — the base can hold thousands of customers, far beyond one turn's page budget, so you would only ever reach a sampled subset and must never claim a complete sweep.

Use `customers_segment_search` instead: it asks Shopify to evaluate the spend threshold SERVER-SIDE and returns ONLY the matching customers plus a server-side `totalCount`, so you get the EXACT, COMPLETE high-value set in one (or a few) bounded pages.

This is how you segment a large store without enumerating it: do NOT page `customers_search` over thousands of customers and filter by hand (you would only reach a sampled subset within one turn, then be tempted to over-claim a sweep you never did).
Each page returns `totalCount` — the server-side count of ALL customers over the threshold across every page.

GROUND your coverage in it: if `totalCount` fits in the page(s) you read (nextCursor=null), you have the COMPLETE high-value set and may say so; if nextCursor is still set you have a partial page — say 'reviewed N of totalCount' and page on.
Each result carries the customer's `amountSpent` ({ amount, currencyCode }), email, name, and numberOfOrders.
CURRENCY: the threshold is compared against each customer's NATIVE lifetime spend in its own `currencyCode` (e.g.
USD).
If the user stated the threshold in a DIFFERENT currency (e.g.

'over 1000 EUR'), you have NO authorized FX rate — the segment is computed against the native figure, so SAY SO ('amountSpent is in USD; the >1000 cut was applied in USD, not converted to EUR — confirm a rate for a strict EUR threshold'); never assume 1:1 parity, never fabricate a rate.

To LABEL these customers (so marketing can target them), match each to a kernel contact by the EXACT email returned here (contacts_search by email) and apply a tag via contacts_write(tags=['high-value']); that produces a filterable TAG (contacts_search(tag='high-value')), NOT a persisted named spend-segment object — there is no agent tool to create a stored Shopify/kernel segment, so describe what you built as a tag, never claim a named segment was saved.
Report ONLY customers this tool returned; never invent or extrapolate a customer or a spend figure.

ORGANIZATION documents must additionally be access-classified: pass an explicit sensitivity, and for 'confidential'/'restricted' pass shareWithRoles naming who may access it (roles_list gives role ids; finance, pricing, margin, revenue and contract material belongs to the executive/C-Level role, NOT org-wide).
Missing placement or access rules returns a structured error listing existing collections so you can retry.

The result includes the new document's id, a `resourceUrl`, and a ready-made `mentionTag` (an @[Title](knowledge:document:<id>) entity tag) — after creating, ALWAYS confirm to the user by pasting the returned mentionTag verbatim in your reply (it renders as a clickable entity pill that opens the doc), never just a bare success sentence.

NEVER FABRICATE DATES OR AN EVENT SCHEDULE INTO A DOC: do not author a document containing SPECIFIC dates (an event/expo/launch start or end date, a 'schedule', a 'calendar', a date-bounded window like 'July 1–14') unless those exact dates came from a source you actually READ (a retrieved Knowledge article, a project task's real due date, an order/invoice).

If the user frames a request with a RELATIVE window ('in the two weeks before the launch', 'in the run-up to the expo', 'until the event') but the SPECIFIC dates are not in any readable source, do NOT search-then-invent and do NOT create a 'Schedule'/'Launch Calendar' doc to fill the gap — manufacturing concrete dates and persisting them here is a fabrication.
Just report the real records you read (e.g. the project's open + overdue tasks) and, for a recurring digest, bound the recurrence with the cron schedule, not with an invented date doc.
Only for an EU buyer in another country with NO VAT number whom the org's data shows as a business: set true when the buyer really is a private consumer (charged their country's VAT).
E-invoicing: who the buyer is. business (a company or a registered professional), individual (a consumer), public_entity, or non_registered_entity.

For a buyer in France it decides whether the invoice is an e-invoice; when nothing on file records it and the call does not say, issuing to a French buyer is refused with customer_kind_missing rather than guessed.
Required when the document is an e-invoice to a French business: line kinds alone never decide it.

A draft may be saved incomplete, but ISSUING refuses without counterparty_name, counterparty_address, counterparty_email and counterparty_country — fill all four before invoice_issue / quote_issue / proforma_issue / po_issue / documents_convert_to_invoice.
Counterparty postal address (freeform, multi-line) shown on the document's Bill-to block.
Set it ONLY when the parcel goes somewhere other than the billing address: the PDF then prints a separate SHIP TO block next to BILL TO.
Leave it null when both addresses are the same (an identical value is not printed twice).
Render only: the tax treatment is still derived from counterparty_country, never from this address.
Consignee name for the shipping (ship to) block, when the parcel is addressed to someone other than the billing customer (a forwarder, a site contact, a reseller's end customer).
Used as a fallback recipient by documents_send_to_customer when the linked contact has none on file.
